_comment: HubSpot pipeline config — committed (no secrets). HubSpot is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for all client/deal activity. Every meaningful communication from Gmail, Slack, Granola, and Lemlist gets logged here as a note on the right deal, and stages are kept current.

internalTracker._note: Where INTERNAL (non-account / SwimScore-ops) items go. The CEO sweep routes account items to HubSpot deals and internal items to this SwimScore Notion board ('SwimScore To-Dos'), a Kanban across seven pillars (incl. Marketing). W2 reconciles items here (dedup on Ref) and checks coverage against the Key Goals database. See SWIMSCORE_NOTION.md.

_stages_note: Verified live against HubSpot get_properties(deals, dealstage) on 2026-07-25 — these are the ACTUAL current stage ids/labels. Re-verify this way before trusting stage names if they're ever suspect again; the board is renamed from time to time without this file being updated.

clinicPartnerships.label: Clinic Partnerships
clinicPartnerships._replyToBeEnriched_note: 2026-08-15, per Shaffy: Lemlist's auto-create automation now lands every fresh reply-triggered deal at 'Reply (to-be-enriched)' (4154315512) instead of landing it directly at 'In conversation (Lemlist)'. This is the new intake bucket — see ingest.enrichment below for what the sweep does with deals sitting here.
clinicPartnerships._earlyFunnelStages_note: 2026-07-25, per Shaffy: the pre-Contracting stages, where a deal is still pure top-of-funnel outreach/qualification. Used to scope the automated Description/Next step refresh (ingest.fieldRefresh) — Contracting-onward deals are managed by hand and the sweep leaves their Description/Next step alone. Extended 2026-08-15 to include the new intake stage.

lemlist._note: Lemlist MCP connected. Read reply threads via get_inbox_conversations + get_inbox_conversation (carries AI interest scoring: aiLeadInterest positive/neutral/negative). Map a positive reply to a stage advance; a negative reply to Closed Lost (with approval). Match the Lemlist lead email to the HubSpot deal's contact.

shopify._note: B2B-ONLY. Inbound messages/inquiries via the Shopify website (www.myswimscore.com contact form, wholesale/clinic inquiries) are often B2B clinic leads — treat them like new-deal discovery: match to an existing HubSpot deal or hand to W0 to create one. Do NOT ingest individual B2C patient orders/customers as deals — B2C is out of scope here. Inbound website messages arrive as emails to info@myswimscore.com (covered by Gmail) and/or surface via Shopify; read both and keep only B2B clinic/partner intent.

ingest._stageMove_note: 2026-07-25: narrowed at Shaffy's request. The sweep now ONLY moves a deal's stage in one situation — see stageAdvanceRule below. Every other stage change (Contracting onward, any close, any manual re-classification) is human-only; the sweep must leave those alone and just log a note.

stageAdvanceRule._note: The ONLY automated dealstage change this workflow is allowed to make. All replies land deals in 'In conversation (Lemlist)' by default; when a Lemlist reply on one of those deals shows real interest, move it forward exactly one step — never skip past 'Demo scheduled', never touch a deal already at 'Contracting' or later (those are updated manually).

toStageOnInfoRequest.label: Asked for information
toStageOnInfoRequest.when: reply asks a question / requests more info / pricing, but hasn't asked for or agreed to a call yet

toStageOnDemoInterest.label: Demo scheduled
toStageOnDemoInterest.when: reply agrees to, requests, or confirms a call/demo/onboarding time

fieldRefresh._note: 2026-07-25, per Shaffy: keep the native HubSpot 'Description' and 'Next step' fields current on early-funnel deals (pipelines.clinicPartnerships.earlyFunnelStages) — these show on the board cards, so both must stay SHORT. Refresh them whenever the sweep writes a [hubspot-ingest] note on one of these deals (not a separate daily pass over untouched deals). Contracting-onward deals are NOT touched — Shaffy manages those fields by hand.
fieldRefresh._nextStepFormat_note: 2026-08-15, per Shaffy: hs_next_step is now a short dated log, not free prose — easier to scan history on the board card. Each line: 'M/D: <what happened>. Next step: <the action>' (no year, no leading zeros — '8/14' not '08/14'). On every touch, PREPEND a new dated line (newest first); do not overwrite prior lines. Cap at the 4 most recent lines (drop the oldest) so the card stays short. One line per date touched — if the deal is touched twice same day, replace that day's line rather than adding a second.

enrichment._note: 2026-08-15, per Shaffy: new step, runs before the normal ingest pass. Lemlist's auto-create automation now lands every fresh reply-triggered deal at 'Reply (to-be-enriched)' (pipelines.clinicPartnerships.stages.replyToBeEnriched) instead of 'In conversation (Lemlist)'. For every deal sitting in that stage: (1) read the Lemlist reply thread and write a [new-deal] note with context (who/company/what they said) same as new-deal-discovery.md §3; (2) set b2bType from the reply/company content; (3) set ordersPmProperty to '1-5' (ordersPmDefault) if no volume signal exists yet — never leave it blank; (4) classify and move the stage using the SAME three-way rule as ingest.stageAdvanceRule (default → In conversation (Lemlist); asks a question/wants info or pricing → Asked for information; agrees to/confirms a call → Demo scheduled) — a deal only stays at Reply (to-be-enriched) if the sweep can't reach it at all (e.g. thread not found); (5) apply fieldRefresh (description + the dated hs_next_step log) same as any other early-funnel deal.

b2bType._note: Infer from the clinic's own description/specialty in the reply or company name — not a guess from the campaign name alone. Leave unset only if genuinely unclear from the content (rare); never blocks the stage move.

enrichment._ordersPmDefault_note: Only default to '1-5' when the thread gives no volume signal. If a patient count/volume is mentioned (e.g. '~250 TRT patients', '5-10/mo'), map it to the closest bucket instead: 1-5, 6-10, 11-25, 26-50, 51-100, 100-200.
enrichment.companyBackfill: orgLinking applies here too — same as the 'In conversation (Lemlist)' bucket, verify/backfill the Company before or when moving the deal off this stage.

declineHandling._note: 2026-08-15, per Shaffy: run this FIRST, before b2b_type/orders_pm/stage-classification — for deals still sitting at Reply (to-be-enriched) only. This is the one narrow, scoped exception to ingest.allowStageClose:false: only this specific pre-human-review intake stage, and only on unambiguous decline language. Never applied to any other stage.

onClearDecline._note: Write the [new-deal] context note (what they said, why it reads as a decline) same as usual, then move straight to Closed Lost. Skip b2b_type/orders_pm/company-backfill — not worth enriching a dead lead. This is the one case in the whole workflow where the sweep sets a close state on its own.

onUncertain._note: Genuinely ambiguous (reads negative-ish but isn't a clean decline, e.g. deflects to a colleague, vague brush-off, sarcastic/unclear tone) — do NOT move the stage and do NOT run the normal positive-path enrichment (b2b_type/orders_pm/classification). Just add a note flagging it's probably not relevant and why, and leave the deal at Reply (to-be-enriched) for Shaffy to move by hand. Mention these in the digest as a distinct 'flagged for manual review' list.

declineHandling._notNegative_note: If the reply is genuinely not a decline (positive, neutral, or a real question), skip this whole block and proceed with the normal enrichment path above (context note, b2b_type, orders_pm, stage classification).

tasks._note: 2026-07-25, per Shaffy: whenever the sweep finds something outstanding on SwimScore's side, create a native HubSpot Task linked to the deal so it shows up in HubSpot's own task queue, not just the note/digest. Applies pipeline-wide (not limited to earlyFunnelStages) — a Contracting-stage deal waiting on us to send a signed agreement deserves a Task just as much as a cold lead waiting on a reply.
tasks._bar_note: HIGH BAR, per Shaffy 2026-07-25: only create a task for something CLEARLY deal-related where we clearly still owe a reply, or a clearly important flag surfaced in email. Do not create one for anything ambiguous, minor, or low-stakes — a task list cluttered with tiny items is worse than useless (erodes trust, gets ignored). When genuinely unsure whether it clears the bar, don't create it; mention it in the digest instead.
tasks._verifyNotDone_note: MANDATORY before every create: re-check the deal's existing notes and the latest activity (email/Slack/Lemlist) for that item specifically — confirm the reply/action hasn't already happened. Creating a task for something already done is exactly the kind of noise that makes the task list untrustworthy.
tasks._defaultOwnerId_note: 162479602 = 'Support SwimScore', the HubSpot user record for shaffy@myswimscore.com (confirmed via get_user_details). This is deliberately different from pipelines/newDealDiscovery.defaultOwnerId (163314964, Syb) — action-owed tasks default to Shaffy.
tasks.subjectFormat: Reply to <name> — <topic>  (or, for non-reply items: <Verb> <what> — <who/what it's for>)
tasks._dedup_note: Before creating a task, search open tasks (hs_task_status != COMPLETED) associated with the deal for one whose hs_task_body already contains the same Ref line — skip creating a duplicate if found. If a prior open task's underlying item is now resolved (evidenced by fresh note content), set that task's hs_task_status to COMPLETED instead of leaving it stale.
tasks.priorityRule: HIGH if the owed item is >7 days overdue or blocks a live deal from progressing; MEDIUM otherwise.
tasks.dueDateRule: Default due date = today (hs_timestamp). Never leave it blank.

slackChannels._note: Channels the daily sweep reads for deal/account + internal signal. Read threads, not just top messages.
slackChannels._newOrders_note: #0-new-order-received — automated Shopify order feed (B2C). Used only for the daily-recap 'Updates from yesterday' order count, never for deal/CRM work — B2C orders stay out of scope for HubSpot.
slackChannels._hubspotInboxLive_note: #hubspot-inbox-live-responses — live feed of the HubSpot conversations inbox (chat/email support). Used for the daily-recap support-question count/pointer, not for deal matching.

staleFollowUp._note: When a deal's LAST CONTACT (most recent inbound/outbound across email, Lemlist, Slack, call) is older than thresholdDays, flag it: add a To-Do to the SwimScore Notion board (New sales pillar) with a SUGGESTED follow-up message drafted from the deal's HubSpot notes/context. Only when a nudge is actually warranted (active/open deal, not Closed; not already waiting on a booked future call). Skip dead/cold-rejected leads.
staleFollowUp._excludeStages_note: Closed Lost, plus everything from 'First order placed' onward — those are converted clients, not open sales pipeline, so a 'New sales' nudge doesn't apply to them.

defaultACV._note: 2026-08-15, per Shaffy: every deal should carry a dollar amount so the board's weighted-pipeline total (bottom of the HubSpot board view = amount × hs_deal_stage_probability, summed) actually means something. Applied as a one-time backfill to all 95 deals that had no `amount` set (2026-08-15), and now applies going forward to every deal this workflow creates or enriches (W0 new-deal-discovery, ingest.enrichment). Never overwrite an `amount` that's already set to something real — only fill it in when blank.

newDealDiscovery._note: Re-enabled 2026-08-11 at Shaffy's request — the sweep creates HubSpot deals again for genuine new opportunities with no existing deal (was disabled 2026-07-25 - 2026-08-11). Company + contact are found-or-created and linked same as before. This block covers opportunities the sweep finds that have NO deal at all yet (e.g. came in via email/Shopify, not Lemlist). Deals the external Lemlist automation already auto-created are handled by ingest.enrichment instead, not this block.

stageAssignRule._note: 2026-08-11, per Shaffy: a new deal never lands anywhere past these two stages — mirrors ingest.stageAdvanceRule's classification, just applied at creation time instead of only to existing 'In conversation' deals.

toStageOnInfoRequest.label: Asked for information
toStageOnInfoRequest.when: the inbound reply itself asks a question / requests more info or pricing

stageAssignRule._demoScheduled_note: Not auto-assigned on creation, even if a call seems implied — Shaffy places a new deal at Demo scheduled by hand when a specific time is actually confirmed (e.g. Improved Health Solutions / Fernando Hernandez, 2026-08-11).

touchTracking._note: 2026-08-16, per Shaffy: track raw touch-level data on every deal so the pipeline shows exactly where each conversation stands, independent of dealstage. Applies whenever the sweep touches a deal with any new development (same scope as ingest's note/field-refresh pass) — not a separate sweep. Backfilled once across the full open pipeline on 2026-08-16.

lastTouchDate._note: Date of the most recent verified touch on the deal from ANY source — email (Gmail), Lemlist reply, or a Calendly booking/acceptance. Always verify directly per the sources block below; never infer from hs_lastmodifieddate, which gets touched by unrelated property backfills (e.g. the defaultACV pass) with no real contact.

lastTouchDirection._note: Direction of that same most-recent touch. Inbound = the contact replied or booked/accepted a call. Outbound = SwimScore sent the last message and hasn't heard back yet. A Calendly acceptance counts as Inbound even though it has no literal message text.

lastMessage._note: The literal text of the last message either side sent. ALWAYS prefix with 'Client:' or 'SwimScore:' so the sender is legible at a glance. If the TRUE last touch (per last_touch_date/direction) is a calendar/Calendly acceptance with no literal message text, last_message must describe THAT event ('Client: accepted the "<event name>" calendar invite for <date>') — NEVER leave the field holding an older, unrelated message just because it's the last one with real text. 2026-08-16 gotcha found in a full-pipeline backfill: several deals had last_touch_date/direction correctly pointing at a calendar acceptance, but last_message was left on a stale earlier message because that's where the text happened to come from — always re-derive last_message from whatever event last_touch_date/direction actually points at, not from 'the last message that had text'.
lastMessage.calendarEventFormat: {Client|SwimScore}: accepted/sent the "{event name}" calendar invite for {date}

initialReplyLead._note: The lead's first-ever reply to our outreach. Set once, never overwritten by later messages (see last_message for the latest).

initialReplySS._note: SwimScore's reply TO that first lead reply — NOT our original cold-outreach copy that started the thread. Leave EMPTY if we have not yet replied to the lead's message; this is an intentional flag meaning a reply is owed. Fill in as soon as we do reply. Call out any deal with this empty in the digest as needing a follow-up.

timeToFirstReplyHrs._note: Our response latency: hours between the lead's first reply and initial_reply_ss (OUR reply to it) — NOT the time the lead took to respond to our original cold email. Leave blank whenever initial_reply_ss is empty (can't compute yet).

replyChannel._note: The ACQUISITION channel — how we originally found/reached this lead (Lemlist email campaign, Lemlist LinkedIn campaign, or a genuine cold call with no prior Lemlist/LinkedIn touch). Set ONCE at deal creation; never overwritten later by a different channel a subsequent touch happens to use (e.g. a demo call held later does NOT change this to 'call').

lemlistCampaignReply._note: The Lemlist campaign name the reply came from (from get_inbox_conversation activity's campaignId, cross-referenced with the #lemlist-replies Slack notification text). Leave blank if the deal didn't originate from a traceable Lemlist thread.

sources._note: 2026-08-16, per Shaffy: determining the true last touch requires checking BOTH Lemlist and Gmail, not just one — a reply sometimes lands only in Lemlist's tracked inbox, sometimes only as a direct Gmail reply to the original sending alias.
sources.checkLemlist: get_inbox_conversation on the deal's Lemlist contactId — the FULL thread, not just the get_inbox_conversations preview.
sources.checkGmail: Search from:/to: the lead's actual email address directly — do NOT route this through 'cc:shaffy' or Shaffy's inbox only. Any SwimScore team sender counts as a real outbound SwimScore touch even when Shaffy is only cc'd for visibility, not the primary sender: info@myswimscore.com, elara.k@maleswimscore.com, stewart.hill@checkswimscore.com, syb@myswimscore.com, or any other *swimscore*/*malescore*/campaign-alias domain SwimScore sends from.
sources.checkCalendly: ALWAYS also search Gmail for Calendly booking/acceptance notifications (from:notifications@calendly.com, from:teamcalendly@send.calendly.com, or subject:"Accepted:") for the contact — a booking can be the true last touch even when Lemlist shows no new reply.
sources._lemlistMislabel_warning: Lemlist sometimes tags SwimScore's own outbound reply-in-thread as an inbound 'emailsReplied' activity (occasionally even with a positive aiLeadInterest score). Read the actual message content and signer, don't trust the Lemlist activity 'type' field blindly for direction.
sources._dateFabrication_warning: 2026-08-16: a full-pipeline backfill found a small number of deals (Allon Health Center, Onto.Health) with a last_touch_date that matched NOTHING findable in Gmail or Lemlist when re-checked individually — the true last touch was actually weeks earlier. Never state a last_touch_date/direction you have not personally seen in a retrieved thread/activity/calendar-notification; if a date can't be pinned to an actual retrieved item, it's wrong. This applies with extra weight to Contracting-onward deals (contracting/portalOnboarding/firstOrderPlaced/activelyOrdering) since Shaffy relies on these for active client status — re-verify those individually against Gmail rather than trusting a single automated pass.

orgLinking._note: 2026-07-25 (2), per Shaffy: a SEPARATE automation (outside this workflow, outside our control) now auto-creates a HubSpot deal for every Lemlist reply. As of 2026-08-15 it lands straight in 'Reply (to-be-enriched)' instead of 'In conversation (Lemlist)' (see ingest.enrichment) — both stages are in scope below since older deals may still sit at the latter. This workflow does NOT create those deals — but whenever it touches one (a note, the enrichment pass, the stage-advance rule, the field refresh), it must first verify the deal has an associated Company, and create+link one if it doesn't. This is a narrow exception to 'never create records': company-only, and only to backfill a gap left by the external deal-creation flow.
orgLinking._scope_note: Checked every time W1 touches a deal in either of these stages — this is literally the 'Lemlist replies, not yet human-reviewed' bucket. Not re-checked on every run for deals that have already moved past both (they were checked once, on the way through).
orgLinking.matchBy: the deal's associated contact's email domain
orgLinking._personalDomains_note: If the only contact email is on one of these, don't create a company from it (same rule as new-deal-discovery.md) — flag in the digest for manual review instead.
